study.question: Can a source-audited, common implementation of aligned full and global rank-half normalization reproduce the previously observed seed42 validation contrast without the unsupported complete-row magnitude correction or failed sparse fallback? Observations: static/pooled/local target-aware AUCs are 0.6050036144838207/0.6102261137080656/0.6133619861190683. Historical aligned full/half AUCs are 0.6149816911798147/0.6151021885074872 (half minus full +0.0001204973276725). Latest global half reproduces the latter aggregate metrics; <=16 fallback drops AUC by 0.0001509840514796 and increases unweighted Logloss by 0.00019345969495585. The tiny 1-16 benefit coexists with worse empty-history ranking and population performance. The current actionable limitation is executable full/half source closure under one implementation, not an established sparse-row or query bottleneck. Independent-seed robustness is still the consequential next scientific question, but this propose interface fixes training seed42 and offers no per-variant seed authority. Final_paired_seeds=[42,43,44] is a final-stage plan, not permission to encode seeds in models.
study.hypothesis: The repeatable no-row global-half advantage is associated with reassignment of detached inverse-product-norm backward scales while preserving recipient tangent direction and fixed-state forward values. A common exported implementation should preserve the signed seed42 half-minus-full contrast. This is a source/reproduction hypothesis, not a new mechanism or independent-seed confirmation. Shared-parameter adaptation, generic conditioning, checkpoint selection, numerical effects and adaptive validation remain unresolved; this contrast alone cannot identify any one mediator. History already contains mechanism-distinct candidates and failures. Further architecture or cutoff search is not justified by the present evidence.
